chapters.heading: Nabota™ key Phase 3 data vs onabotulinumtoxinA

content.text: A prospective, multicenter, **randomized, double-blind, active- and placebo-controlled**, single-dose study
To assess **efficacy** and **safety** of prabotulinumtoxinA vs onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo

**The non-inferiority of prabotulinumtoxin to onabotulinumtoxinA was confirmed** at Day 30 using the definition of a responder as a patient with a glabellar frown line severity score of 0 (none) or 1 (mild) as assessed by the investigator
**Fast treatment onset** was demonstrated by 54.2% of prabotulinumtoxinA patients exhibiting a ≥1-point improvement from baseline at Day 2 compared with 8.3% of patients in the placebo group
**Long duration of action** was demonstrated by 37.7% of prabotulinumtoxinA patients exhibiting a ≥1-point improvement from baseline at Day 150 compared with 12.2% of patients in the placebo group

**Changes in psychological wellbeing** were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)-A and HADS-D scales which measure anxiety and depression. There were statistically significant mean changes from baseline to Day 90 of –1.1 and –0.6 for HADS-A and HADS-D, respectively, indicating an improvement following treatment
**Comparable safety profile to onabotulinumtoxinA** with no statistically significant differences between the active groups for the most common events (headache and nasopharyngitis)

A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Dose, Phase III, Non-Inferiority Study Comparing PrabotulinumtoxinA and OnabotulinumtoxinA for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Glabellar Lines in Adult Patients

chapters.heading: 1. I like the fact that Nabota™ is made for aesthetics with Hi-Pure™ Technology

content.text: **Purity is important** to patients today as they care deeply about what is in the cosmetic products and treatments they undergo with an increasing desire for ‘**healthy**’ and ‘**clean**’ products, particularly among millennials¹

Merz Aesthetics developed BOCOUTURE® which is the ONLY highly purified toxin only containing the 150kd active neurotoxin, **XTRACT™ technology is used** it its manufacture to remove **other clostridial proteins** which have no therapeutic purpose but constitute an unnecessary foreign protein load²
**Nabota™ contains complexing proteins** which, unlike the neurotoxin, can be recognized by the immune system and stimulate an immune response **risking the generation of neutralizing antibodies**²,³
A formulation purified from complexing proteins like **BOCOUTURE® poses the lowest risk of neutralizing antibody formation** and therefore of secondary treatment failure²,³

**Background information:**
• Recent consumer research in beauty and personal care, showed that 72% of respondents said it was important to purchase healthy or clean products¹
• The manufacturing process of BOCOUTURE® involves several chromatographic steps to purify the neurotoxin from the complexing proteins while minimizing the risk of denaturing, degrading or losing biological activity of the neurotoxin²
• The neurotoxin itself does not contain any molecular signatures recognised by dendritic cells which may stimulate an immune response while the complexing proteins do, and are therefore identified as adjuvants³
• Neutralizing antibodies can result in partial or complete treatment failure²

chapters.heading: 2. I’ve heard that Nabota™ has a rapid onset of action

content.text: In the study by Rzany and colleagues, the percentage of patients treated with prabotulinumtoxinA with a ≥1-point **improvement from baseline on Day 2** assessed by the investigator **was 54.2%**, compared with 12.2% for placebo¹
A rapid onset of action is an advantage in an aesthetic procedure contributing to patient satisfaction

Clinical trials have not compared the onset of action of Nuceiva™ with BOCOUTURE® but studies have confirmed the **rapid onset of BOCOUTURE®**. In a trial comparing BOCOUTURE® with Botox® and Dysport®, the median onset of action in males and females was assessed by physicians compared with baseline videos **and occurred two days earlier** in those treated with BOCOUTURE® **compared with the other two products²**

Another key factor contributing to patient satisfaction is continuing treatment success. Unlike BOCOUTURE®, **Nabota™ contains complexing proteins** which can be recognized by the immune system and stimulate an immune response **risking the generation of neutralizing antibodies which can lead to secondary treatment failure³,⁴**

Background information:
• In the non-inferiority study by Rzany and colleagues, onset was investigated by exploring the percentage of patients with an improvement at Day 2 rather than exploring the effect over time¹
• In the Rappl study (n=180), onset was defined as an improvement of ≥1-point from baseline on the 5-point Merz Aesthetics Scale when comparing muscle activity assessed by the injecting physician and one other physician²
• Median time to onset for BOCOUTURE® was 3.02 and 3.36 days for females and males and for Dysport® was 5.32 and 5.93 days, respectively²

chapters.heading: **3. Nabota™ is almost equivalent to Botox®1**

content.text: **Relative efficacy** of different treatments can only be assessed in **head-to-head trials**
Not only has **BOCOUTURE®** been shown to be **non-inferior to Botox®** for the treatment of glabellar frown lines², it has further been proven to be **equipotent to Botox®** in that indication³

**Nabota™** has only demonstrated **non-inferiority to Botox®** in a Phase 3 study for the treatment of glabellar frown lines⁴ and so far there are **no published data investigating the equivalence of Nabota™ and Botox®**
Patients and clinicians want a treatment with **known and reliable effects**. **BOCOUTURE®** has been used for over 15 years and has over 200 publications

items: The Sattler study (n=381) assessed 24 U BOCOUTURE® or Botox® for the treatment of glabellar frown lines with responders defined as those with a ≥1-point improvement from baseline. Non-inferiority of BOCOUTURE® to Botox® was confirmed at Week 4²
The Kane study aimed to demonstrate the equipotency of 20 U Botox® and BOCOUTURE® for the treatment of glabellar frown lines (n=250)³

In the Nuceiva™ study vs Botox® and placebo (n=540), patients were treated with 20 U of each toxin and non-inferiority was confirmed for the primary endpoint of responder rates at Day 30 where a responder was a patient with a score of none or mild on a 4-point scale⁴

chapters.heading: **4. Nabota™ will appeal to my patients as it is cheaper than Botox®1**

content.text: **Reports have suggested that, per unit, Nabota™ will cost 20–30% less than Botox®1**

Depending on your market, pricing conversations can consider **duration of action** and its impact on the long-term cost of treatment or the **benefits of a pure toxin** which some patients would be willing to pay for

**Treatments with a long duration of action are preferable in terms of long-term cost** and in a study by Kerscher and colleagues, a single 20 U treatment of **BOCOUTURE®** had a **median duration of action of 177 days which is approximately 6 months2**

Purity matters to patients and influences their choice of brand. Unlike Nabota™, **BOCOUTURE® is free from complexing proteins and has been shown to have a low risk of neutralizing antibody development**, which may be related to its low protein load and lack of complexing proteins3
**Reducing the risk of developing neutralizing antibodies and secondary treatment failure with a pure toxin maximizes the potential to provide patients with a lifetime of treatment**

**Background information:**
• With an expected cost per unit of between $8 and $16, Nabota™ would be cheaper than Botox® ($10 to $20 per unit) with a saving of between $40 to $80 for each treatment based on a standard 20 U dose1
• Kerscher and colleagues assessed treatment duration as the time between injection and the return to baseline severity (n=151)2

chapters.heading: **5. Nabota™ seems to appeal to my young patients who are asking to be treated with it**

content.text: The **indication** for both Nabota™ and BOCOUTURE® specifies **adults <65 years** of age so the target patient population is the same in terms of age for both products¹,²

Young patients who may desire a lifetime of treatment with a botulinum toxin may benefit from a pure product like BOCOUTURE®, which is free from complexing proteins, and therefore **poses the lowest risk of neutralizing antibody formation** and consequently of secondary treatment failure³,⁴

Patients, particularly perhaps the younger ones also care about sustainability. A further benefit of **BOCOUTURE®** is its **stability at room temperature** for 3 years, eliminating the need for a cold chain, cold storage materials and their disposal²

In a study comparing **estimated greenhouse gas emissions** associated with secondary shipping packaging of BOCOUTURE® – which can be shipped without a cold chain – and Botox®, which requires refrigeration, standard shipments of Botox® were estimated to generate **approximately 90 times more greenhouse gas emissions** than BOCOUTURE® shipments⁵

items: The stability of BOCOUTURE® at room temperature means it can be transported and stored without refrigeration which is good for the environment

The study by Thistle, estimated that the total greenhouse gas emissions of secondary packaging were 0.0389 kg-CO₂e for BOCOUTURE® and 3.5705 kg-CO₂e for Botox®. It was estimated that for every 1000 shipments, this difference equated to the use of over 1500 L gasoline⁵

chapters.heading: **Appendix 2: Nabota™ key Phase 3 data vs placebo: Study design**

items: Ten different sites in the US in each trial (20 study centers in total)

Healthy adults at least 18 years old with moderate to severe glabellar frown lines at maximum frown independently agreed by investigator and subject assessments using a 4-point photonumeric scale for glabellar frown lines
Day 0 randomization 3:1 to receive treatment with either 20 U prabotulinumtoxinA or placebo as an injection of 0.1 mL into each of 5 sites)
A total of 330 subjects in EV-001 and 324 in EV-002 were randomized to treatment and received treatment

For the primary efficacy end point, according to the composite end point of investigator and patient assessed improvement of ≥2 points from baseline, responder rates for prabotulinumtoxinA vs placebo were 67.5% vs 1.2% and 70% vs 1.3% in EV-001 and EV-002, respectively.
Using the composite end point, secondary endpoints at Day 90, Day 120 and Day 150 also demonstrated the superiority of prabotulinumtoxinA over placebo.
Exploratory end points of ≥1 point improvement from baseline or a score of 0 or 1 at maximum frown also clearly showed differences in response between prabotulinumtoxinA and placebo

In terms of safety assessments, the overall incidence of adverse events, the incidence of the most common event and the incidence of study drug-related events were similar between prabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups. No serious adverse events were study-drug related
Limitations of the studies include the low number of patients from subpopulations of interest such as those ≥65 years, men, non-Caucasian ethnic groups and individual Fitzpatrick skin types
The aim of this study by Song and colleagues (n=42) was to determine the safety, efficacy, and onset of action of prabotulinumtoxinA (20 U total dose) for the treatment of glabellar frown lines
Improvement in glabellar frown lines was observed in 85.4% and 51.2% of subjects 2 days after administration at maximum frown and at rest, respectively

chapters.heading: **Appendix 3: Nabota™ key Phase 3 data vs onabotulinumtoxinA: Study design**

items: Nineteen different sites in France (5 sites), German (7 sites), Sweden (2 sites), UK (1 site) and Canada (4 sites)

Healthy adults at least 18 years old with moderate to severe glabellar frown lines at maximum frown assessed by the investigator using a validated 4-point photonumeric scale for glabellar frown lines. In addition, patients must have answered yes to the question: Do you find that your glabellar lines have an important psychological impact, for example, on mood, anxiety or depressive symptoms?
Day 0 randomization 5:5:1 to receive treatment with 20 U prabotulinumtoxinA, 20 U onabotulinumtoxinA or placebo as an injection of 0.1 mL into each of 5 sites
A total of 540 subjects were randomized to treatment and received treatment (245 prabotulinumtoxinA, 246 onabotulinumtoxinA and 49 placebo patients)

The responder rates at Day 30 (where a responder was defined as a patient with a score of 0 or 1 as assessed by the investigator at maximum frown on the 4-point glabellar frown lines scale) were 87.7%, 82.8% and 4.2% in the prabotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups, respectively

The absolute difference in responder rates between the prabotulinumtoxinA and onabotulinumtoxinA groups was 4.4% (95% CI were −1.9, 10.8). Given that the lower bound of the 95% CI was greater than −10.0, noninferiority of prabotulinumtoxinA to onabotulinumtoxinA was confirmed
Patient-assessed responder rates using the same definition at Day 30 were 78.8%, 76.0% and 6.3% in the prabotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups, respectively

Subject satisfaction was high with responder rates (where responders were those with ≥1-point improvement in the subject satisfaction scale from baseline) of 91.3%, 86.6% and 6.3% in the prabotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups, respectively, at Day 30
Patients randomly assigned to prabotulinumtoxinA achieved statistically significant improvements in Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)-A and HADS-D
The overall incidence of adverse events as well as the most common events were not statistically significantly different between the active treatment groups
